lesson_title: A Tonne of Rock, a Gram of Gold
hook_text: Miners blast a whole tonne of rock to get a few grams of gold. How does that become a ring?
clip_script: Welkom, in the Free State goldfields. Deep underground, some mines go down more than three kilometres. Miners drill and blast gold-bearing rock. A tonne of rock may hold only a few grams of gold. At the plant, the rock is crushed and the gold is separated and melted into bars, then refined in Germiston. A jeweller melts, rolls, shapes and polishes it into a ring. Rock to bar to ring: value added at every step.
visual_style: Whiteboard cross-section of a deep mine shaft, rock moving up to a crushing plant, a glowing gold bar, then a ring on a jeweller's bench.
mood: Impressive and careful, like watching a skilled craft.
pacing: Steady descent into the mine, a rising journey to the surface, then fine detail at the jeweller's bench.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and look for the carat stamp inside a piece of gold jewellery at home.
